newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan, Israel disagree over joint airport.
newsitem.headline: Jordan, Israel disagree over joint airport.

text.p: Negotiations between Jordan and Israel on building a joint airport near the Red Sea coast hit a deadlock on Thursday over Israeli security concerns, a Jordanian official said.

"They want a terminal inside Jordanian territory to be under their control but this is unacceptable. It is not possible to give up Jordanian territory," said a Jordanian official close to the talks which were held in Jordan's Red Sea port of Aqaba.

The idea of the joint airport was to ease congestion at Israel's Eilat airport, which is nine km (five miles) north of Aqaba airport, and help Jordan tap new traffic through a newly built passenger terminal close to it and an expanded runway.
U.S. Lockheed Martin had completed last July a feasibility study for a proposed $80 million international airport serving Aqaba in Jordan and Eilat in Israel.
But Israeli transport officials presented their Jordanian counterparts with new radically modified proposals which undermined the project's principle, the official told Reuters.
"They presented us with a proposal that demolishes the Lockheed terms of reference...they want a solution that solves their technical problems at our expense," the official said.
A decision on the new Israeli proposals would be taken at a higher political level, he added.
The planned airport is one of several joint projects, approved in the spirit of optimistic cooperation which followed a 1994 peace treaty between Jordan and Israel.

Officials say Israel's enthusiasm for the project, which was agreed to and strongly supported by the previous Labour government, appeared to wane after a rightwing government came to power in Israel last year.
Israeli officials, who say that they are not opposed to the airport plan in principle, however expressed fears it could be an expensive political gesture rather than a viable comercial venture.
